note: Consumer genetics. Status disputes the prefilled public float: 23andMe filed for Chapter 11 on 2025-03-23 and TTAM Research Institute completed the purchase of substantially all its assets on 2025-07-14 (Wikipedia, 23andMe); the listed shell was renamed Chrome Holding Co. and deregistered (EDGAR 15-12G, December 2025). Insolvency followed by an asset sale reads acquired with the business continuing under TTAM (decisions D8). The Sequoia row still reads public at the 2024-09-30 float; this row holds the fresher cited evidence. Entry: Google Ventures was already an existing investor at the November 2010 Series C led by J&J Development Corporation (TechCrunch) and at the December 2012 Series D (the company's release). GV was formed in 2009, after the 2007 Series A that Google itself bought (D2: not a GV position), so its first round was the 2009 Series B ($27.8M, of which TechCrunch reported $2.6M 'from Google' in June 2009); a Series B reads Growth. City follows the Sequoia row (South San Francisco, Oyster Point) as the last operating headquarters.

Personal profile pages. AOL bought About.me in 2010 and spun it back out in February 2013 with $5.7M led by True Ventures, Google Ventures among the investors (TechCrunch, 2013-02-05). TechCrunch's June 2014 report calls the $11M Foundry-led round the Series B and 'its second since getting spun out', which names the 2013 round the Series A. Acquired by Broadly in February 2019 (TechCrunch; the firm's own exit line).

funding_rounds.round: unnamed (spin-out financing; the next round is named Series B)

note: Real-time expense management (YC W14), acquired by Certify in July 2018 (TechCrunch; the firm's own exit line). Country disputes the Wikidata DE claim: that match is a different Abacus; this one is US (New York, as the YC row places it). No source read names the round GV entered (its partner M.G. Siegler is on the firm's 2014-2015 pages), so the stage is undetermined. The Menlo row named Abacus is a different company (a 2025 tax-document startup), a name collision; the YC row is this company and still reads private, which the Certify acquisition overrides.

Deception-based threat detection (Santa Clara). Accel led the Series A (September 2015) and Ignition the Series B (June 2016), $17M combined, with no GV (TechCrunch, 2016-07-26). GV invested in November 2016, bringing total funding to $22M (the company's release, 2016-11-03); an unnamed investment after a Series B reads Growth.

Oncology small molecules targeting RNA-modifying proteins (Lexington, MA). GV joined as a new investor in the $63M Series B led by EcoR1 Capital (the company's release, 2020-04-23) and is listed among the existing investors in the $75M Series C led by Mirae Asset (2024-01-23). Still operating (2026 releases); no priced mark near $1B.

COVID antibodies; renamed Invivyd (NASDAQ: IVVD), whose EDGAR business address is New Haven, CT. The S-1's related-party tables show entities affiliated with GV buying Series A preferred in July 2020 ($5.5M of the $49.9M), then Series B ($20M) and Series C ($7.5M). Market cap $280.02M on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), which replaces the 2025-06-30 float.

A 'cognition API' (persistent memory and knowledge graph for AI agents), founded November 2022 by Adam Ghetti and David Bader, based in Austin; it launched from stealth in July 2026 having raised $17.8M to date from GV, Bond Partners, Hillspire and others (Upstarts, 2026-07-14). The report names no round, so the stage is undetermined; the entry date is the firm's own first Invested month (2026-07, decisions D7). Momentum slice check 2026-09-28: no priced round at or near $1B on the record; $17.8M raised in total and no valuation disclosed.

Mobile ad targeting (Boston). Matrix Partners led the $2M seed (TechCrunch, 2012-03-13); Google Ventures led the $10M Series A (TechCrunch, 2012-12-04). Acquired by Time Inc.'s Viant in January 2017 (TechCrunch; the firm's own exit line).

Antibody discovery platform in Lebanon, NH (the Form D address). Still operating in 2026 (partner GSK's depemokimab approvals, April 2026 release); no priced round or listing at $1B on the record. The stage stays the prefilled Form D band.

Protein nanoparticle delivery for genetic medicines (Feng Zhang). The company's launch release (2023-02-16) says it raised '$193 million in combined Series A and B financings led by ARCH Venture Partners, GV and Lux Capital'; the firm's own post says the financing was co-led by GV. The release does not split the two rounds, so the Series A is read at medium confidence. City: the company's site gives Cambridge, MA (read 2026-09-28); the Lux row's Boston follows the release's dateline.

funding_rounds.lead: ARCH Venture Partners, GV, Lux Capital

note: Rationally designed AAV gene therapies (Waltham, MA). The S-1 lists GV among the investors in the $110M Series B of April 2021; the Series A tranches went to the existing Series A investors, and GV is named only in the B. The 2022 IPO was not completed; the company announced a Series C in October 2025. No mark at $1B.

Gas fermentation turning industrial CO2 into chemicals, spun out of DTU and based in Copenhagen. It raised a $10M seed in February 2023 from ACME Capital, GV and Atlantic Labs (TechCrunch, 2023-11-30), then a $43M Series A co-led by HV Capital and GV (ESG Today, 2024-07-18). No mark at $1B.

Autonomy and tele-assist for farm tractors (South San Francisco). It came out of stealth in September 2021 with a $4M seed from Grit Ventures, GV and Village Global, then took a $5M seed extension (TechCrunch, 2022-01-18). The Series A closed at $32.8M in October 2024, led by Autotech Ventures (The Robot Report), which graduates the seed.

Protein made from CO2 by microbes (Pleasanton, CA). The $32M Series A was led by ADM Ventures, Barclays and GV (AgFunderNews, 2021-01-07), GV's first appearance on the firm's list the same year. No later priced round or mark on the record.

Sean Parker and Shawn Fanning's group video app. Its first round, $8.3M from Founders Fund, Accel, Andreessen Horowitz, Google Ventures, SV Angel and others (TechCrunch, 2012-03-25), preceded the $25M second round led by Kleiner Perkins (Wikipedia, Airtime.com); a 2011 first round of that size is the Series A, as both sibling rows read it. Status aligned with the a16z and Sequoia rows (wound down after its relaunches). City follows the a16z row (New York, where the relaunched app was run); the Sequoia row says San Francisco, the 2012 base.

Neurodegeneration immunology (NASDAQ: ALEC), EDGAR business address South San Francisco. GV 2014, L.P. and GV 2017, L.P. signed the Series E registration rights agreement filed with the S-1, and the S-1 lists GV among its investors, but no source read ties GV to the round it entered (the firm has listed Alector since 2015), so the stage is undetermined. Market cap $214.38M on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the 2025-06-30 float.

Regenerative-farm meat sold direct to consumers from Iowa, Wisconsin and Minnesota farms; the site still sells (read 2026-09-28). 99 Counties, Inc. (incorporated 2021) filed one Form D, first sale 2022-02-08, $3.72M sold, from Keystone, IA, with no GV person among the related persons. No source read ties GV to a round (Andy Wheeler is on the firm's 2022 people page), so the stage is undetermined.

Accountable-care network for independent primary care practices (Bethesda, MD). GV joined as a new investor in the $20M Series B1 led by Biomatics Capital (Healthcare Dive, 2017-01-10) and returned in the $64M Series C (Crunchbase News, 2020-04-20). Mark: the $260M Series F led by Lightspeed, which 'values the company at $3.5 billion, Bloomberg reported' (Crunchbase News, 2023-06-23), the same mark as the IVP and Lightspeed rows; older than 24 months, so stale. The December 2025 $500M was a credit facility, not a priced round.

AI detection of disinformation and narrative attacks (dateline Washington and New York). Its $20M Series B was led by GV with Ballistic Ventures, closed late 2023 (the company's release, 2024-10-30); the firm's own first Invested month, 2023-11, dates it (decisions D7). Momentum slice check 2026-09-28: no priced round at or near $1B on the record; the Series B is the last round found and no valuation was disclosed.

Multi-cloud network as a service (San Jose). It came out of stealth with about $30M from Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins in April 2020; Koch Disruptive Technologies led the $54M Series B in October 2020 'plus a new investor, GV Management Co.' (SiliconANGLE, 2020-10-13); Tiger Global led the $100M Series C (TechCrunch, 2024-05-15). Lumen Technologies completed its acquisition on 2026-07-07 (citybiz; press reports put the price at $475M). The Sequoia row still reads private; this row holds the fresher cited evidence.

Virtual care for women's chronic hormonal conditions (New York). The firm's own post of 2023-10-18 reveals 'our latest investment' and says the company is 'announcing $10 million in Series A funding led by GV'. Index Ventures led the $26M Series B with 'existing investor GV' (the company's release, 2025-01-24, dateline New York).

AI supply-chain and trade intelligence (New York; the Form D address is Brooklyn). After a $7M seed (TechCrunch, 2020-11-24), GV led the $15M Series A (AlleyWatch; Amadeus Capital says the round closed in May 2021, the firm's own first Invested month). Mark: the $200M Series C led by the US Innovative Technology Fund 'values the company at $1 billion', GV an existing investor (Crunchbase News, 2024-07-29), exactly at the band edge; older than 24 months, so stale. Momentum slice check 2026-09-28: no later priced round found (July 2026 news covers Altana buying Cervo).

Social VR platform, acquired by Microsoft in October 2017 and shut in March 2023 (Wikipedia, AltspaceVR). The firm's own post (2022-10-03) calls it 'an early GV seed investment'. By June 2015 it had 'absorbed $5.2 million' from investors including Google Ventures (TechCrunch, 2015-06-12), then raised an unnamed $10.3M round led by Comcast Ventures (TechCrunch, 2015-07-29). No source read dates the seed, so no entry date is given; the $10.3M round falls just short of twice the $5.2M and carries no round name, so it does not decide the column. City follows the Lux row. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Sales-team performance and gamification software (YC W14), founded in Chattanooga, TN (TechCrunch, 2014-02-21). Country disputes the Wikidata MA claim, a name-match on a one-word name. Its seed came from The Lamp Post Group, Y Combinator and YC VC, without GV (TechCrunch); the firm lists Ambition from 2016, and no source read names the round GV entered, so the stage is undetermined. A Series B from Primus Capital was reported in October 2021 (Business Journals headline).

AI sorting robots for recycling, Louisville, Colorado (as the Sequoia row places it). GV joined the $55M round with XN and Valor in January 2021 (Business Wire headline); later rounds include the $91M Series C (November 2022); no priced round or reported valuation at $1B on the record.

Podcast creation and hosting (New York). Country disputes the Wikidata GB claim: Anchor was a New York company. Accel led a $2.8M round in March 2017; GV led the $10M Series A (TechCrunch, 2017-09-28, 'The New York-based team is announcing $10 million in Series A funding, led by GV'). Spotify acquired Anchor in February 2019 (TechCrunch). The YC row named Anchor is a different company (a Lagos banking API), a name collision.

Global engineering talent marketplace, founded in Lagos, headquartered in New York (as the Spark row places it). Country disputes the Wikidata LV claim, a name-match. Spark led the $10M Series A (2015); the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative led the $24M Series B, and 'Venture firm GV also joined the round, alongside existing investors' (Techpoint Africa, June 2016), so GV entered at the B; GV returned in the $40M Series C (TechCrunch, 2017-10-10). Mark: the September 2021 Series E led by SoftBank 'values the company at $1.5 billion' (Rest of World, 2021-09-29), which replaces the unicorn-list source with a cited one and settles the name match; older than 24 months, so stale. Same mark as the Spark row.

Startup fundraising and fund-administration platform. Google Ventures co-led, with Atlas Venture, the $24M round of September 2013 at about $150M (TechCrunch, 2013-09-23; the round was first reported nine months earlier). The record names the March 2022 $100M round led by Tiger Global the Series B (Wikipedia, AngelList), which makes the 2013 round the Series A (medium confidence). Mark: that 2022 round 'valued the business at $4.1 billion' (TechCrunch, 2022-03-12, AngelList Venture, the fundraising business the firm's listing describes); older than 24 months, so stale.

funding_rounds.round: unnamed (the next named round is the Series B)

note: Anchored cytokine immunotherapy for cancer (the company's site gives 245 Main St, Cambridge, MA). GV was among the new investors in the $45M Series B, alongside existing investors Polaris Partners and Mithril Capital (the company's release, 2021-11-12). Still reporting clinical data in 2026; no mark near $1B.

Threat intelligence platform (Redwood City), founded 2013 as ThreatStream. Stage disputes the prefilled Form D band (Growth on the 2018 filing): ThreatStream 'raised $4 million in Series A funding from investors led by Google Ventures' (TechCrunch, 2014-02-20), and General Catalyst led the $22M Series B in December 2014 (TechCrunch). The 2018 filing is a later round Karim Faris sat on as a director. Still private; its rounds price it well under $1B (about $96M raised by 2018 per Wikipedia).

Topical therapies for HPV lesions (South San Francisco). The $31M Series D was led by Adjuvant Capital 'and joined by GV, formerly Google Ventures', a new investor (the company's release, 2021-11-02); GV is an existing investor in the $53M Series E led by MPM-BioImpact (2023-04-27). Reporting clinical data in 2026; no mark near $1B.

In-app customer feedback for mobile apps (Seattle). It raised $1.2M 'in seed funding from Founder's Co-Op, Google Ventures, Social Leverage, Golden Venture Partners' (TechCrunch, 2012-12-10), then a $5.3M Series A led in part by SurveyMonkey (TechCrunch, 2014-09-25), which graduates the seed. Acquired by Alchemer in 2023 (the firm's own exit line).

Mobile A/B testing (YC S13, San Francisco). Its $2.1M seed named Merus Capital, Google Ventures, Oliver Jung and an AngelList syndicate as the biggest investors (TechCrunch, 2014-01-22); a $4M Series A followed (TechCrunch, 2015-02-17), which graduates the seed, as the a16z row records. Acquired by Airship in August 2019 (TechCrunch).

Automated mobile app testing on real devices (San Francisco). TechCrunch names the $4.5M round of May 2013 a Series A (2013-05-28) and VentureBeat says Appurify 'raised $4.5 million from Google Ventures last year' (June 2014); no source read places GV in the 2012 seed the Felicis row enters at, so the entry is the Series A (medium confidence). Google acquired Appurify in June 2014 (TechCrunch).

Mobile app performance monitoring, formerly Crittercism (San Francisco, Wikipedia). Crittercism raised $12M in Series B financing 'led by Google Ventures, with contributions from existing investors, Shasta Ventures and Opus Capital' (TechCrunch, 2013-03-12), so GV entered at the B; a $30M round with Accenture followed in April 2014. Acquired by VMware in 2017 (the firm's own exit line; SiliconANGLE headline, May 2017).

Immuno-oncology (NYSE: RCUS; EDGAR business address Hayward, CA). Band disputes the prefilled float: the market cap is $3.18B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), against a $565.9M float of 2025-06-30. The S-1's certain-transactions tables show GV 2016, L.P. buying $25M of the August 2016 Series B and GV 2017, L.P. buying Series C in November 2017; GV holds no Series A.

Oral dexpramipexole for eosinophilic asthma, created by Knopp Biosciences and Population Health Partners. A syndicate 'led by Bain Capital Life Sciences with participation from Access Biotechnology, GV, ARCH Venture Partners' and others committed up to $350M in Series A financing (Bain Capital release, 2022-07-12); an additional $75M of Series A followed in February 2024. The company's own site (read 2026-09-28) describes it as 'formerly based in Chapel Hill, NC' and 'no longer operating', so it reads defunct at its last headquarters.

Autonomous AI offensive-security agents, founded by Kevin Mandia (dateline San Francisco). It announced $189.9M 'in Seed and Series A funding', 'Led by Accel, with participation from Google Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, Menlo Ventures, In-Q-Tel, and follow-on investment from 8VC and Ballistic Ventures' (the company's release, 2026-03-10). The follow-on wording marks 8VC and Ballistic as the seed's investors, so GV and the other new names read as Series A investors (medium confidence), as the Accel and Menlo rows read their own entries. City follows the release and the Menlo row; the Accel row says Menlo Park. Momentum slice check 2026-09-28: no priced round at or near $1B on the record; the company is not disclosing its valuation (TechCrunch, 2026-03-10).

Immuno-oncology (pegilodecakin), Redwood City per its S-1. The S-1's certain-transactions tables show GV 2014, L.P. buying 2,860,194 shares of the Series C sold in closings of November 2015 and February 2016 ($7.5M of $49.5M), and GV holds no earlier series. IPO January 2018 (NASDAQ: ARMO); Eli Lilly agreed to acquire it in May 2018 for about $1.6B (Lilly's release, linked from the firm's own listing; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Eli Lilly, 2018').

Small molecules that target RNA (Waltham, MA). Canaan Partners led the $38M Series A without GV (2017-02-27); venBio and Nextech co-led the $75M Series B 'with participation by new investors Omega Funds, HBM Healthcare Investments, GV (formerly Google Ventures)' and others (the company's release, 2019-04-18). Still operating (CEO change June 2026); no mark near $1B. The Accel row named Arrakis is a different company (a London AI-agent startup), a name collision.

Antibodies against infectious disease, Waltham, MA per its S-1. Status disputes the prefilled public float: Arsanis merged with privately held X4 Pharmaceuticals in 2019 and its listed entity (CIK 1501697) now carries the name X4 Pharmaceuticals (EDGAR lists Arsanis, Inc. as its former name); the firm's own line reads 'Acquired by X4 Pharmaceuticals, 2019'. Successor-entity ambiguity reads acquired with a successor note; the float belongs to X4's business. Entry: GV 2016, L.P. signed the investors' rights joinder dated 2017-04-24, the month of the Series D financing, and holds 1,540,499 shares from preferred (S-1); the S-1's 5%-holder tables do not list GV among the Series D buyers, so the Series D reads at medium confidence.

Recorded family-story interviews (heyartifact.com). The company's own site (read 2026-09-28) announces 'Artifact is shutting down', no longer sells new Artifacts and hosts completed interviews through 2024, so it reads defunct. City from the site's 415 (San Francisco) phone number. The firm lists it from 2023 (M.G. Siegler); no source read names a round, so the stage is undetermined. The a16z row named Artifact is a different company (a speedrun fintech in New York), a name collision.

Autologous cell therapy for Parkinson's (San Diego, per the company's site). The $147.5M Series B was 'Led by GV, LYFE Capital and Revelation Partners' (the company's release, 2022-05-09); the firm lists Aspen from 2022. A $115M Series C followed in November 2025 (Fierce Biotech and Endpoints, linked from the company's site). No mark near $1B.

Targeted cell depletion for chronic disease (San Carlos, per the company's site). Stage disputes the prefilled Form D band (Growth on the $43.3M filing of 2024-09-16): that filing is the round the company named its $43M Series A (Business Wire, 2024-10-09), and the band's anchor, director Vineeta Agarwala, last appears on GV's pages in 2019 and signs as Andreessen Horowitz's partner (T4: the seat is not GV's). The seed Form D (first sale 2021-12-17, $7.5M sold) lists only the CEO; a16z says it 'first invested in Arda at the Seed' and led the Series A. GV is named in the Series A release, but its body could not be read (Business Wire, Morningstar and Endpoints refused), so whether GV entered at the seed or the Series A is not established: undetermined. No mark near $1B.
